text: What you're seeing here is a test animation made from still illustrations in the Bear Draws AI style. A sketchy, abstract blend of ink, geometry, and character exaggeration that leans heavily on line work and minimal color splashes. It's a visually clever aesthetic, great for editorial cartoons or conceptual storytelling. But translating it into motion using imagetovideo tools like Runway, V3, or Cling can be tricky. Why? Because not all still images animate well. This style relies on flatness and dense line detailing, and many AI video tools struggle with interpreting that into coherent motion. You might see flickering, broken limbs or melting geometry. Sometimes the character's expressions warp or their proportions

Collapse. If you're working with art like this, test it first. Don't assume it will animate cleanly. You may need to redesign characters with clearer silhouettes or simplify the style for better results. Clean outlines and larger contrast zones tend to animate more smoothly in AI models. Also, if you're using runway, note that it often drops the resolution significantly. To fix that, consider upscaling the final video using a tool like Topaz or Magnific AI for sharpness and detail restoration. Bottom line, if you love your art, try it anyway, but be prepared to adjust. Animation with AI is part experiment, part improvisation. And if you found this useful or inspiring,
Like, subscribe, and share it forward because artists helping artists is the algorithm we all need.
